title: Serde default external-tagged encoding of HeaderValueTyped is now part of the public contract
description:
header_typed.rs:152-170 — HeaderValueTyped derives Serialize + Deserialize with no `#[serde(...)]` attributes. The default serde encoding of a Rust enum is externally-tagged:

    HeaderValueTyped::Addresses(vec![...])  ⟶  {"Addresses": [...]}
    HeaderValueTyped::DateTime(None)        ⟶  {"DateTime": null}
    HeaderValueTyped::Raw("hi".into())      ⟶  {"Raw": "hi"}

This JSON shape is now part of the public contract — callers who persist these types in databases, transmit them over JSON-RPC, or write them to message queues now depend on it. Changing the representation is breaking.

Plausible future changes that would be breaking:

- Internally tagged form: `#[serde(tag = "form")]` → `{"form": "Addresses", "...": ...}`. Matches JMAP wire format better.
- Adjacent tagged form: `#[serde(tag = "form", content = "value")]`. Also closer to JMAP.
- Snake_case or kebab-case variant names via `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`. JMAP uses camelCase (`asAddresses`, `asMessageIds`).
- Renaming a variant (e.g., DateTime → Date) — already prevented by #[non_exhaustive], but Serialize/Deserialize derives doubly lock the wire tag.

Caller-facing consequence: a JMAP server serializing these for transport over the wire is locked into the rustic serde default representation, not the JMAP §4.1.2 wire format. A future "JMAP-native" version is breaking for current callers.

Same concern applies to HeaderForm (line 130): its serde encoding is the default `"Raw" | "Addresses" | ...` — capitalized Rust enum names, not the JMAP `asRaw | asAddresses | ...` strings.

Fix options:
- Accept the current shape and document it ("HeaderValueTyped serializes as externally-tagged JSON; for JMAP wire format, callers should map separately").
- Add `#[serde(rename = "as...")]` on each variant and re-evaluate the tag style now while pre-1.0.
- Provide a dedicated JMAP-shaped serializer in a separate module.

Either commit to the current shape in writing, or fix the shape now before downstream code calcifies on it.
close_reason: Documentation batch on the typed header surface: (.7) parse_header_typed now states trailing CRLF is permitted-but-not-required (matching the implementation); (.8) EmailAddress.name and AddressGroup.name field docs now state the trim+empty-to-None normalization; (.12) HeaderValueTyped doc has a Serde Wire Format section pinning the current externally-tagged shape and explicitly distinguishing it from RFC 8621 wire format (callers responsible for that mapping); (.17) parse_header_typed doc now carries one runnable example per HeaderForm variant (six total); (.24) HeaderDateTime has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is field-wise not instant-wise, with a worked example and the to_timestamp escape hatch; (.25) EmailAddress has an Equality Semantics section noting derived PartialEq is byte-exact (no RFC 5321 domain case-folding) and pointing callers at manual canonicalisation; (.30) parse_header_typed doc has an Empty-Result Ambiguity table making explicit that callers cannot distinguish malformed-vs-empty-vs-non-UTF-8 and flagging the future-direction (strict variant / warnings tuple). No code changes.
